## Desktop

### Improvements
- OpenCode 1 now offers the upgrade to OpenCode 2.0. OpenCode 2 downloads in the background and installs only when you choose: Restart to upgrade, Upgrade on quit, or Later. Your sessions, projects, and settings are kept. Plugins made for OpenCode 1 need an update.

versions.name: v5.1.72
versions.body:
**A thread send now reaches a session that is not running, on this device or on another of your devices, and starts it.** It needs senpi 2026.11.15-2 or later (omo pins it), and device service 0.1.31 or later on both devices for a wake from another device. A reply to a sender on another device reads only that device's sessions instead of the whole account listing; a send to a live session that is paused or holds a Stop answers `queued` with `waiting_on: { kind: "hold", device }`; and `waiting_on.kind` in a `thread_send` result can be `approval`, `hold` or `wake`. ([#13599](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/13599))

### Changed

- `omo remote enable` now sets the device up in one command after `omo login`. It installs the OmO device service when none runs, registers this omo's agent dir with it, turns remote sessions on, and installs and starts the always-on session host unit. If you signed in before the device service was installed, it also links that sign-in to the service, so `omo login` then `omo remote enable` leaves the device connected. Running it again changes nothing that is already in place (#13594). ([#13602](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/13602)) ([#13606](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/13606))
- `omo remote status` also shows this device's own units as the service manager reports them: the session host unit (running, enabled, pinned host), the device service's unit, whether the cold-wake entry is in place, and the agent dir omo registers. With `--json` these are a `local` object beside the status fields (#13594). ([#13602](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/13602)) ([#13606](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/13606))
- Thread gateway: waking a session that is not running is on (#13037). It runs on senpi 2026.11.15-2 or later (omo now pins it), the release whose session release drops a woken session's retained record. A message from another of your devices wakes a session here once both devices run device service 0.1.31 or later. The local omo daemon (`omo daemon run`, or the device service's cold-wake unit) registers this device's agent dir with the device service and takes deliveries as soon as it starts, with no session open. ([#13599](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/13599))
- Thread gateway: the operator daemon declares the delivery consumer as soon as it loads omo, with no session open (#13037 cold wake). `omo daemon run` sends the daemon it ensured senpi's `warm`, so a daemon the device service starts on demand can be handed deliveries before any session runs. A warm that is refused or unsupported prints one line and the run still exits 0. ([#13596](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/13596)) ([#13599](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/13599))
- Thread gateway: the session wake loads from its own sidecar (`extensions/omo-wake.js` behind `#omo-wake-runtime`): the carrier, the delivery consumer and the device-service client never enter the main `omo.js` bundle, which carries only lazy shells; the ensured host's idle-exit setting is read inside the sidecar. ([#13456](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/13456)) ([#13599](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/13599))
- Thread gateway: waking a session that is not running needs no setting (#13037). A `thread_send` from this machine to a session here that is not running now starts it by default, and the answer is `queued` with `waiting_on: { kind: "wake" }`. `session_wake.same_device` stays in the configuration schema only as an explicit opt-out (`false`), read for the target session's own project. The wake starts on senpi 2026.11.15-2 or later (senpi#6449), which omo now pins. ([#13456](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/13456)) ([#13599](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/13599))
- Thread gateway: when no operator host is running, a session that is not running still starts (#13037). Before it opens the session, the carrier asks the engine's own `host ensure --policy never`, from omo's daemon launch spec, on the socket `thread_create` uses. A running host is reused whatever its build; one is started only when nothing answers. The ensured host runs with `omo daemon`'s own host environment: the agent directory is named (`OMO_AGENT_DIR`) and the configured `task.host_idle_exit_ms` rides along (`SENPI_RPC_HOST_IDLE_EXIT_MS`) instead of the launch spec's default, and from a source tree the launch spec resolves to the plugin's tracked copy so the CLI is always handed a file that exists. ([#13456](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/13456)) ([#13599](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/13599))
- Thread gateway: a delivery from another device is no longer gated on the device service's wake switch being told on. While this engine's delivery consumer is served (from its serving acknowledgement, before its startup pending sweep, so a remote row that sweep wakes is never told the gate is off), the carrier opens the session. The consumer serves on senpi 2026.11.15-2 or later with device service 0.1.31 or later, and it no longer reads the wake the service tells: the wake switch it tracked (`wakeAllowed`, the `delivery.wake` event) had no production reader left. ([#13456](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/13456)) ([#13599](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/13599))
- The delivery consumer (design 5.4) runs beside the carrier. The engine minimum for a woken session, `MIN_WAKE_ENGINE_VERSION` (A8.1, senpi 2026.11.15-2, the release that drops a released session's retained record), gates the carrier as well. A device service older than 0.1.31 does not carry the delivery protocol, so on it the consumer serves nothing and does not ask again. ([#13455](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/13455)) ([#13599](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/13599))
- The gateway store's schema moves to version 12: three nullable columns on deliveries and a unique index on the new ledger id. The first process on this release migrates the store; any process still on the previous build then reports the store's "schema too new" error on its thread tools and inbox drain until it restarts. ([#13208](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/13208)) ([#13279](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/13279)) ([#13599](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/13599))
- Thread gateway: once a build carrying this store ships, every gateway store open runs the schema step to version 13 (one new table, `woken_sessions`) and raises the store's `user_version` for good. An older build, or a rolled-back one, that shares the same agent directory then refuses to open that store with its "schema too new" error until it is upgraded again. ([#13212](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/13212)) ([#13279](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/13279)) ([#13599](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/13599))
- A reply to a message that came from another of your devices goes to the session on that device that sent it, whether you reply by its session id or by the name it gave. A session on another device, or on this one, that only carries the same id or name no longer receives the reply. ([#13218](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/13218), part of [#13037](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/issues/13037)) ([#13599](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/13599))

### Fixed

- An omo engine on a device whose device service runs on a non-default `--state-dir` now registers with it: `deviceServiceStateDir` takes a non-empty absolute `OMO_DEVICE_SERVICE_STATE_DIR`, then the `device-service.location.json` discovery file beside the default dir, and only then `~/.omo/device-service` (#13597). ([#13598](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/13598)) ([#13606](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/13606))
- A remote worktree remove refused for an empty reflog now says reflogs may be off in the repository, instead of claiming they are: an expired or deleted reflog looks the same (#13542 follow-up). ([#13546](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/13546)) ([#13606](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/13606))
- Thread gateway: the session wake keeps working after the session that started it ends (#13037). The carrier and the delivery consumer are one per agent directory for the whole process, but they used the first session's gateway store, which that session's shutdown closed, so every later wake in the process failed. The running wake now opens its own store for the life of the process. ([#13596](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/13596)) ([#13599](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/13599))
- Thread gateway: the carrier re-checks the sender's peer admission at the moment of every open of a row from another device (#13456 review follow-up), so the retry and lease-takeover paths - which the accept-time check of the consumer and the before-turn check of the drain bracketed but nothing else covered - start nothing when the answer is refused or unknown. A lease takeover now consults the same allowance a wake does, ending its record when nothing queued allows the open; the runtime answers the carrier's admission ask on the live delivery port, so the startup pending sweep's own wakes are admitted too. ([#13511](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/13511)) ([#13599](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/13599))
- Thread gateway: the session wake loads from its own sidecar (`extensions/omo-wake.js` behind `#omo-wake-runtime`): the carrier, the delivery consumer and the device-service client never enter the main `omo.js` bundle, which carries only lazy shells. ([#13457](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/13457)) ([#13599](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/13599))
- Thread gateway: a consumer failure that changes kind (a device that answers nothing and then refuses the declaration) is warned again: the retry loop's one-warning rule is keyed on the failure itself, not on merely being down, and still stays silent while the same failure repeats. ([#13457](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/13457)) ([#13599](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/13599))
- Thread gateway: the delivery consumer listens before it declares itself, so the records the device service hands it right after the acknowledgement are no longer dropped. It counts as serving from that acknowledgement, so a session it wakes during its own start is opened, not left switched off. ([#13457](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/13457)) ([#13599](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/13599))
- Thread gateway: the delivery consumer is started again after it dies (#13457 review): a device service that answers nothing, refuses the declaration, or restarts under a served connection no longer leaves remote wake off for the engine's life. A failed start closes its port and reports itself, a connection that ends during the startup sweep leaves no stale serving consumer behind, and a connect failure the client reports is logged instead of dropped. ([#13457](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/13457)) ([#13599](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/13599))
- Thread gateway: the wake switch the service tells (`delivery.wake`) has no reader since the carrier's gate moved to the consumer serving, so the consumer no longer tracks it. The conformance fakes the production-port test uses are now a package export of `device-service-core` instead of a deep path into its test tree. ([#13457](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/13457)) ([#13599](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/13599))
- Thread gateway: a delivery id that the same device repeats after its 30-day receipt expired, while its row is still in the store, is answered from that row as deduplicated instead of failing with a raw unique-constraint error (the review of #13208). ([#13212](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/13212)) ([#13279](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/13279)) ([#13599](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/13599))
- Thread gateway: a session whose file header cannot be read, or names a session kind this build does not know, is never started or reopened unattended. It is refused like a child or worker session instead of being treated as an ordinary interactive one (#13037). ([#13279](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/13279)) ([#13599](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/13599))
- When another device refuses to wake a session there that is not running, the reason its delivery consumer gives is shown only when it is a short machine code; any other reason is shown as `unrecognised`. ([#13277](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/13277), part of [#13037](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/issues/13037)) ([#13599](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/13599))

### Added

- `omo remote bootstrap` and `omo remote enable` install and start one fixed, always-on per-user unit beside the OmO device service that runs the omo session host: the systemd user unit `omo-session-host.service` on Linux (enabled, restarted after every exit) and the LaunchAgent `ai.omo.session-host` on macOS (run at load, kept alive). It runs `omo daemon run --pinned` for the registered agent dir, and the device service's `OMO_RELAYD_SERVICES` table names it (entry `"omo"`) as the only unit it may start for a cold wake. The table keeps its other entries, and the device service restarts only when the table changed. `omo remote disable` disables and removes both, and while remote sessions are off a bootstrap removes them instead of installing them (#13594). ([#13595](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/13595)) ([#13606](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/13606))
- `omo daemon run --pinned` starts the operator host with no idle exit; a task host started from one of its sessions still idles out as usual (#13594). ([#13595](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/13595)) ([#13606](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/13606))
- Device service client: the delivery-consumer requests of #13037 (`deliveries.serve`, `delivery.answer`, `delivery.held`, `delivery.pending`, `delivery.drained`, `peer.admitted`) and their events (`delivery.inbound`, `delivery.holds`, `delivery.wake`), in the shapes omo-relay-daemon #1076 ships, behind `connectDeliveryConsumer` in `device-service-core`. The conformance fixtures are copied in-tree from that release. ([#13457](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/13457)) ([#13599](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/13599))
- Thread gateway: the engine's delivery consumer now connects to the device service through that client, so a delivery from another device for a session here that is not running is taken in, answered, and the session started. ([#13457](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/13457)) ([#13599](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/13599))
- Thread gateway: the session wake now loads from its own sidecar, `extensions/omo-wake.js` behind `#omo-wake-runtime`: the carrier and its host connection, the delivery consumer and the device-service client never enter the main `omo.js` bundle, which carries only three lazy shells (the session-start start, a send's same-device wake, the control endpoint's admission ask); a sidecar that fails to load answers as if no wake exists. Measured 1,547,852 -> 1,476,860 bytes on this branch; the byte ceiling in `bundle-budget.json` moves to 1,478,000 for it. ([#13455](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/13455)) ([#13599](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/13599))
- Thread gateway: the session wake of #13037 now runs in production, but only on an engine at or above the wake engine minimum `MIN_WAKE_ENGINE_VERSION` (A8.1): the first engine release that drops a woken session's retained record (senpi#6449). Below it no carrier starts, and a `thread_send` naming a session that is not running answers as it did before the wake existed (`queued_offline` with `reason: "wake_unavailable"`). At or above it, every `tui` or `rpc` engine (never a task child, never under CI) starts one carrier per agent directory on its first session start: it opens the session by path on the operator host that `thread_create` opens on, sends the engine's `wake`, and hands it back quietly once it has finished; the answer is then `queued` with `waiting_on: { kind: "wake" }`. It still follows `session_wake.same_device`, read for the target session's own project, which stays off by default. ([#13455](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/13455)) ([#13599](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/13599))
- Thread gateway: the carrier sweeps its woken rows on a timer only while the table holds a row (design A3.1.4: an empty table leaves no timer). ([#13455](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/13455)) ([#13599](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/13599))
- Thread gateway: a session's own inbox drain admits nothing while a carrier is opening it (A3.1.5). It asks the device service whether a row's sending device is admitted before it takes in a delivery from another device (5.6). ([#13455](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/13455)) ([#13599](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/13599))
- Thread gateway: the store can take in a delivery that another device's service attested for a session on this device that is not running (the intake row of #13037). The row is committed in the same transaction as a same-device delivery, keeps the sender's delivery id, text and display text, is rate-limited per sending device, and is admitted later under the engine's own ledger key, so the engine counts it once even if the same delivery also arrives live. A repeat of a delivery id from the same device is answered with the first answer. A reply to such a delivery continues its chain. ([#13208](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/13208)) ([#13279](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/13279)) ([#13599](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/13599))
- Thread gateway: the store keeps a record of each session a wake asked for or opened (#13037): one row with its state, a lease and a generation that fences every write, at most 4 such sessions past `requested` per agent directory, and a transient open failure that returns the row to `requested` with its attempts and the time of the next one (the third deletes it). A wake primitive resolves a durable id to its one session file, refuses child and worker sessions, ensures the host and sends one plain `open_session` frame (no `attended`, no permission preset). ([#13212](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/13212)) ([#13279](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/13279)) ([#13599](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/13599))
- Thread gateway: the pieces that will let a message from another of your signed-in devices reach a session that is not running on this device are the delivery consumer, the carrier that opens such a session in its own working directory and hands it back when its turn is done, and the pending sweep (#13037). ([#13220](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/13220)) ([#13279](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/13279)) ([#13599](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/13599))
- `omo remote wake [on|off|default]` reads or sets whether sessions on this device that are not running may be started by a message from your other signed-in devices; `default` follows the build's default, which is off. It needs device service 0.1.31 or later; on an older one the command sends nothing and says so. ([#13257](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/13257), part of [#13037](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/issues/13037)) ([#13599](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/13599))

versions.body:
**Plain `omo login` signs a computer in from the terminal while OmO accounts are closed.** A computer with no OmO desktop app — a server over SSH, a fresh Linux box — runs `omo login`, gets a device code to approve on another device, and stores the credential in the OS credential store; the attach-before-mint refusal (#13096) answers a computer that already has its device before anything is asked of the service. The success line names the signed-in account (`Signed in to OmO as <email>.`), and `omo whoami` names it too; a failed account read still says how to see it. `omo logout` and `omo whoami` run while closed, so no message names a command that refuses. `login --help` describes the route (the command stays hidden from `omo --help`), every other closed `login` form refuses with a message that names the route, the closed hints name both routes, and the compiled entry classifies bare `login`, `logout` and `whoami` as one-shot launches with the same shared parse the command uses (`login --` included). The damaged-item message names the terminal route too instead of a desktop-app-only dead end. Tests run the flow through the npm launcher (against a service-auth bundle built from this source into a temp copy of the launcher tree), the compiled entry and the toolkit CLI, with an isolated HOME and runtime dir, no inherited session bus, an injected store, and a refusal-text assertion on every zero-mint case. ([#13281](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/13281)) ([#13328](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/13328))

**The computer-use conformance preflight tests pass on Windows.** The missing-driver message now prints its repo-relative path with forward slashes on every OS, so a run reads the same on every host, and the stdio-probe test builds its stand-in engine as a real executable for the host instead of a POSIX shell script. QA tooling only; no runtime behaviour changes. ([#13295](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/13295), part of #13221)

**Computer use gets a declared-outcome conformance catalog for its QA.** `script/qa/computer/conformance/` adds a typed catalog in which every action, toolkit and mode cell on each OS declares that it delivers or refuses with an exact engine code, a report that fails a missing, duplicate, skipped or mis-coded cell or one that disturbed the person's session, an environment preflight that ends a broken host's run as `ENVIRONMENT_ERROR`, and twelve model-free reference tasks. versions.body:
**OmO runs on senpi 2026.11.10-2.** A client can read and edit the workspace's instruction files over RPC through `read_project_file` / `write_project_file` (senpi#6307), a built session can be parked and handed out through `claim_session` (senpi#6350), the Fable 5.2 prompt preset gains the codebase-ownership sentence (senpi#6360), `generate_image` is eval-only like `bash` (senpi#6272), eval cells reach every eval-only tool through `tool.<name>(...)` and the `agent()`/`output()` helpers (senpi#6276), and the EQ goldens carry the new prompt (senpi#6355). ([#13054](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/13054))

**An agent that answered a message from another agent can keep answering it in the turns the engine starts on its own, with no prompt.** The reply allowance a consumed delivery grants (a reply to that sender by id or stated name, approved from the delivery alone) now lasts for the work the delivery started: the consuming turn and every later turn the engine starts by itself - an open-todo reminder, a goal continuation, a monitor wake. A settle alone no longer ends it; it ends when a new message starts work after that answer: a person's message, or any delivery, whose own sender the new group then holds (a delivery that joins running work adds its sender). A reply in a covered turn continues the delivery's chain at the next hop, so the chain limit still closes it. ([#13042](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/issues/13042), part of #12996) ([#13044](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/13044))

**`omo remote send` now goes through the same delivery pipeline as every other send, and `--steer` reads the session once.** A person's message to a session on another device enters `createDeliveryPipeline` with the relay address book's reference for the `<device>/<session>` address, so the CLI no longer builds its own transport call; the relay transport reads the running turn once and steers it, where the CLI used to read it a second time first. A `--steer` to a session that is running nothing still sends nothing. The unused second prompt implementation (`promptRemote`) and its argument check are removed. Which sender kinds each device admits is unchanged. ([#13038](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/13038))

**A message to a session on this device that waits on a question now says so, as one to another device does.** The send is still queued, and its `delivery` now carries `waiting_on: { kind: "approval", device }`. `device` is this install's account device, and is absent when the install has no device identity. ([#13035](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/13035))

**Every message one session sends another now names the device it was sent from, on this device and across devices alike, and a message from another device counts as the cause of the receiving run's next send the same way a local one does.** When no device id can be read (no device service, or it does not answer), the message still goes and records why it names no device. ([#13034](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/13034), part of [#13004](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/issues/13004))

**A message sent or handed off to a session on another device now reports its `delivery_id`, `effective_mode` and `endpoint`, as one sent within this device does.** The answer came from the account's session listing and dropped those fields. It now passes the relay transport's own delivery facts through. The `endpoint` is `null` because the sender knows no endpoint on that device. ([#13033](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/13033))

**A reply to an agent on another device now reaches it by the id in the message header or by its name, with no prompt on the same account.** One resolver now finds a thread across this device's threads and the account's other devices: an exact durable id, then an account alias, then the name ladder judged over every entry (two devices sharing a name are an ambiguous_target naming both devices, never a silent pick). `thread_send`, `thread_handoff`, the control tools, `thread_create` (open or fork) and the `omo thread` CLI all use it. A reply to the sender of a delivery the run took in is approved from that delivery alone - by the sender's durable id or the name it stated - and must resolve to that sender, else it is refused as `reply_target_mismatch` without sending. The id shown for a thread on another device is its durable id; the relay listing carries it when the device publishes one. The `omo remote` verbs still dispatch by the id you type as the device's session key, so pass the id the device lists under until that path moves onto the shared resolver. ([#13000](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/13000))

**A send to an agent on another device now reports the same facts as one on this device.** `thread_send` and `thread_handoff` answer `delivery_id` and `effective_mode` for a target on another device too, so a caller reads the delivery's id and the lane it took the same way whichever device holds the thread; `message_seq` and `endpoint` stay the facts of a gateway row on this device, and `device` names another one. The reply allowance (a run answering the agent whose delivery it took in, by that agent's id or stated name, with no prompt) is proved identical for a same-device and a cross-device delivery, and one parity table now runs every send assertion against both legs, so a rule that reads the transport fails the build instead of reaching a user. ([#13006](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/issues/13006), on top of [#13000](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/13000))

**A task child no longer starts against a senpi engine that refused its process-wide redaction registry; the start fails with `SenpiEngineRestartRequiredError`, which says to restart omo.** The engine refuses to load next to a registry slot it did not install, and that refusal lasts for the whole process, so a restart is the only remedy. ([#12991](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/12991))

**omo now installs the signed device service 0.1.27 instead of 0.1.3.** The device service pin had stayed at 0.1.3 across every device-service release since 0.1.3, and an installed omo only replaces a service older than its pin, so no machine received a newer one. ([#12981](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/12981))

**The `thread_*` tools are now eval-only, like `bash`: when an eval tool is present they are no longer in the model's direct tool list and are called as `tool.thread_*()` inside an eval cell.** Behaviour, permissions and results are unchanged, and without eval they stay ordinary direct tools. ([#12907](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/12907), closes [#12903](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/issues/12903))

**A long-running engine keeps reclaiming crashed one-shot memory runs.** The memory component's cleanup of abandoned one-shot runs, which runs once per engine process outside session opens, now repeats once a day in an engine that stays up, such as the desktop's or a daemon host's, instead of waiting for a restart. ([#12899](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/12899))

**Opening a session no longer re-sweeps the memory root.** The memory component's cleanup of abandoned one-shot runs now runs once per engine process, shortly after the first open, instead of inside every session open. A session that ends before that cleanup starts hands it to the next open, so crashed runs are still reclaimed. ([#12896](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/12896))

### Fixed

- The senpi barrel load-failure test imported the barrel by a pathname-derived `/D:/...` specifier, which failed on Windows and turned dev red (#13068). It now imports the barrel by file URL. ([#13068](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/13068))
- Computer use reports a click or typed text that went out as window events with its real input route, and judges whether input landed only for multi-event input such as drags, so a single click whose window then closes is reported delivered. ([#13055](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/13055))
- The actionability check no longer refuses `press` on a Linux button that lists only another action such as `click`, since the backend presses its first action. ([#13055](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/13055))
- Computer use flags text typed into a secure field of a background window, and reports how much text was delivered when the user intervenes mid-send. ([#13055](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/13055))
- On macOS, key priming now bounds and classifies its focus reads, so a slow or failing focus read no longer stalls background typing into a multi-window app. ([#13055](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/13055))
- Computer use keeps holding the machine-wide interaction lock while it hands key focus back after background typing, so another session can no longer type in between. ([#13055](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/13055))
- A steer sent to a session on another device that was held behind that session's open draft, and whose turn ended before the draft was released, was answered `queued` and then lost without a word (#12927). The send now records that refusal: a retry of the same send under the same `idempotency_key` answers `turn_conflict`, naming the delivery, instead of `queued`. ([#12935](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/12935))

### Changed

- Computer use now lets the user keep typing and clicking while it works by default (`computer.intervention: "continue"`); set it to `"pause"` to have input wait for the user and stop with `UserIntervened`. ([#13055](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/13055))
- While computer use waits for an accessibility target to become actionable, other computer-use sessions of the same user can keep sending input instead of being refused `InputBusy`; the target is checked once more, without waiting, right before the action. ([#13055](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/13055))
- Desktop engine: the stop-marker policy is pinned to the XPC-only path and reported by `omo doctor`. ([#12831](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/12831))

### Added

- Computer use waits until an accessibility target is actionable before it acts, lists the sheets, windows and menus an action opened, suggests the next call when it refuses, and refuses `cmd+q`, `alt+f4` and `win+l` unless the key chord is forced. ([#13055](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/13055))
- Wayland (Hyprland): window-targeted pointer input through libei behind a `windowInput` capability probe (`no_eis`, `hyprland_ipc_missing` reasons). ([#12831](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/12831))
- Wayland (KWin): window-targeted pointer input through the same libei path, and window captures placed on the KWin frame rectangle so coordinates round-trip between capture and click. ([#12831](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/12831))
- `senpi-desktop-sdk`: the typed facade package for computer-use v2 consumers (connect, Computer / Window / Element / Frame, reports and verification, typed errors), with a pinned facade manifest and a package-boundaries test. ([#12831](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/12831))
- Desktop engine: `skeleton` observation (logical depth 3), the web-wrapper rule, and `root: <ref>` drill with sub-generations (object mode only). ([#12831](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/12831))
- `senpi-desktop-sdk`: the spawn transport with the in-session refusal (`spawn_inside_session`); the service run facade routes windows, displays and capabilities through the SDK. ([#12831](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/12831))
- Desktop engine host: features-gated session.open options (intervention, macosKeyPriming, trace, reportMode) sent only when the engine advertises them; `ActionReport` typed exec results with the 7 valid disposition pairs; reserved settings `computer.run_sandbox`, `intervention`, `macos_key_priming`, `trace` (defaults unchanged); error codes `COMPUTER_AMBIGUOUS_TARGET`, `COMPUTER_CAPTURE_CONSENT_REQUIRED`, `COMPUTER_PROTECTED_PROCESS` with `data.reason` hints. ([#12831](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/12831))
- Desktop engine: late replies after a stop are quarantined (`Suspended`, disposition `unknown / unknown`, audited on stderr); macOS helpers (overlay, keymap, canary) gain parent-death containment. ([#12831](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/12831))
- Desktop service: a fresh-process permission re-probe before every session open, so a capture/accessibility grant made after a denial is seen without restarting the service. ([#12831](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/12831))
- `computer.run`: a QuickJS cell with wall-clock, call and payload limits and an escape battery (no host bridge yet). ([#12831](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/12831))
- macOS capture: SkyLight-first window capture with SCK/legacy fallback, capture of windows on another Space, and a measured replayd consent probe (opt-in, never gating). ([#12831](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/12831))
- Desktop engine: epoch sources (display change, lock, sleep, Space switch, engine restart) announced as `epoch.changed`; stale frames after an epoch move answer `InvalidCoordinateFrame superseded`. ([#12831](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/12831))
- Desktop engine: the ref-generation store keeps 8 live generations per target and up to 65,536 retained objects; refs past their generation answer `StaleRef`. ([#12831](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/12831))
- Desktop engine: object-mode `ax.snapshot` returns a partial observation (`complete`, `nodesObserved`, `cuts`) at a 3000 ms default deadline and a node budget; null mode is byte-equal to v1. ([#12831](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/12831))
- Desktop engine: per-stage timings on action reports and a redacted trace JSONL sink, both behind the `trace` session option (default off). ([#12831](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/12831))
- Wayland (KWin): window-targeted pointer input through libei behind the `windowInput` capability probe, plus the KDE QA driver. ([#12831](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/12831))
- Kernel `computer` globals (JS and Python preludes) are generated from the SDK facade manifest; `verify` lives on the desktop root, `drill` on window handles. ([#12831](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/12831))
- Wayland (GNOME): window-targeted pointer input through a small Shell extension that publishes the window list over the session bus. ([#12831](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/12831))

versions.body:
**`omo thread` says when a broken install leaves it on this device only.** A thread client sidecar that cannot be loaded no longer makes `omo thread read <alias>` silently answer `not_found`: stderr names the sidecar, the error, and the reinstall step. The CLI sign-in's own warnings (a retired trust pin, a failed device-service forget) now reach stderr too. ([#12936](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/12936))

**A message to a busy thread now reaches the turn it is running, by default.** `thread_send` and `thread_handoff` with no delivery mode (and `omo thread send` without `--mode`) steer the recipient's running turn and start a turn when it is idle, on this device and on another device alike; a message queues behind the running turn only when the caller asks for `follow_up`, or when the turn cannot take a steer (a waiting question, a compaction, an engine that reports no turn epoch). A send that steers a turn ending at that very moment falls back to the lane the target has then instead of failing. ([#12921](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/12921), part of [#12879](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/issues/12879))

**OmO runs on senpi 2026.11.9-2.** A tool that an eval cell awaits no longer leaves the running cell blank for a moment when it finishes: its streamed lines stay until the cell's own output or its result replaces them (senpi#6257). ([#12920](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/12920))

**`omo remote send` now travels the same road as a session's `thread_send` to another device, and every reply from another device is explained by one mapping.** The person at a terminal who sends to a session on another device goes through the relay transport (the same offline check, the same steer preflight against the running turn, a receipt in this device's gateway store) while keeping their own prompt record; what the user reads when a command on another device is refused (`omo remote`, the attach TUI, the thread tools and the SDK) comes from a single module, so a device that did not answer, a missing grant or an uncertain result reads the same everywhere. ([#12911](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/12911), part of [#12879](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/issues/12879), fixes [#12885](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/issues/12885))

**OmO runs on senpi 2026.11.9.** It brings senpi's `admit_external_message` (a message relayed from another device's session is admitted as an ordinary delivery) and makes a relayed delivery read exactly like a same-machine one, with the device kept in its metadata only. The one-channel relay transport (#12879) needs both. ([#12904](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/12904))

**The Install button on omo.dev's header no longer presses against or slips past the pill's right edge.** The floating nav bar gives its last control the same inset as the logo on the left, and below 1000 px the section links move into the menu so nothing is pushed outside the pill in any language. ([#12893](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/12893))

**A thread an agent creates or forks with `thread_create` now starts in the creator's own approval mode on this device too, not the host's default.** A session created on another device already did (#6189); the two legs now run one body: a name is checked against the device the thread lands on (a name that device already lists live is `name_conflict` there), opening a thread that is live on another device answers that thread without opening it again, and the created thread's facts (name, working directory, timestamps) come from the engine's reply on both devices. ([#12891](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/12891), part of [#12879](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/issues/12879))

**Stopping, closing, renaming, re-modelling, changing the reasoning level of, or reading a thread works the same way whether that thread runs on this machine or on another device of your account.** `thread_set_reasoning` now reaches a thread on another device too, and a session with no file yet that another client still holds answers the same on both. ([#12890](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/12890), part of [#12879](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/issues/12879))

**A message an agent sends to a session on another device now arrives there exactly as a message between sessions on one device.** The receiving session gets a delivery entry (never a user message) with the same sender line and authority notice a same-device delivery carries, deduplicated under the same key, and it wakes on receipt the same way; a reply is just another send back. Nothing in the delivered text names the device it crossed, and `omo remote send` from a terminal is unchanged. A send from `omo thread send` to a session on another device is refused as data (the engine admits a command-line delivery only from its own machine) and points at `omo remote send`. ([#12889](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/12889), part of [#12879](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/issues/12879), fixes [#12882](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/issues/12882), fixes [#12877](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/issues/12877), fixes [#12346](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/issues/12346), fixes [#12865](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/issues/12865), fixes [#12857](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/issues/12857))

**Sending a message to another session now goes through one delivery pipeline whether that session is on this machine or on another device.** The device difference is a transport module behind one port; nothing a user sees changes in this release. ([#12887](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/12887), part of [#12879](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/issues/12879))

**A message to a session on another device now reads exactly like one from a session on the same machine.** The receiving agent sees which session sent it, not which device, and replies by that session as usual. ([#12878](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/12878))

**A subagent whose model takes more than 90 s to start answering is no longer aborted by runtime fallback.** With `runtime_fallback` enabled, the first-prompt watchdog cut every subagent that showed no progress within a fixed 90 s and re-prompted the fallback model, so reasoning-heavy models that legitimately think longer before their first token were killed and their prompt was sent twice. The watchdog now waits 300 s, the same stream-start bound the engines use, and `runtime_fallback.first_prompt_timeout_seconds` sets it (`0` disables it). ([#11893](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/11893), fixes [#11887](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/issues/11887))

### Fixed

- `omo thread send` to a thread alias held on this device now reaches that thread when run from another workspace, the same way `omo thread read` does, instead of answering that no visible thread matches. ([#12860](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/12860))
- Memory shutdown drain: the session-shutdown wiring no longer claims senpi puts no bound on its handler. senpi bounds one `session_shutdown` handler with its own warn threshold, per-handler timeout and total quit budget (shipped defaults 2 s / 10 s / 2 s, each user-tunable and 0-disableable), and the 1500 ms drain budget is sized under those defaults and pinned by a test that reads them from the installed senpi, so a host release that lowers a default below the drain fails there. No host cap was added from OmO and nothing bypasses the host abort; a journal flush skipped by the budget still raises its error-level alarm. ([#12795](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/12795), refs [#10336](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/issues/10336))
- The browser skill's docs and examples teach BrowserSkill 0.4 shared control for the omowright it now ships (`^0.3.0`): every gated page action carries the context of a fresh `session.cooperate("sync")`, and a `cooperation_sync_required` refusal waits for the person with `session.cooperate("wait")`, then re-syncs and replans. They also note which calls are gated, that a gated action throws a `TypeError` on an unknown option key (with the two calls that pass stray keys through instead), and that `page.on("dialog")` listeners receive a `Dialog` they can answer. The omowright this release ships includes running-browser discovery through `DevToolsActivePort`, `goto` on sparse and frameset pages, UTF-8 decoding across BrowserSkill IPC chunks and unique-only stale-ref recovery (thanks @ashmoonori-afk, code-yeongyu/omowright#115 to #118), and agent tabs in their own window (thanks @devxoul, code-yeongyu/omowright#120). ([#12494](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/12494))
- The senpi-task cold-revive residency test is now bounded by the product's own liveness rules instead of a flat 20 s total (Part of #10993). A Windows child that blocks for a while during startup no longer fails it unless the product would also give up, and a real stall fails with the last stage it reached and the stall length. The test's child also reports senpi's startup phase timings, so the next block names its phase. ([#11706](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/11706))

### Changed

- Skills: `ulw-research` and mass research in `mass-ulw` now require every conclusion to rest on something a tool actually observed. Workers tag claims `OBSERVED:` and dead ends `PROBED:`, anything known only from memory is sent back as a lead, and mass-research verify nodes re-open each observed source. Both research editions state the rule in their opening contract, and every mass-ulw node prompt carries it in its VERIFY item. ([#12832](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/12832), fixes [#12830](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/issues/12830))
